newsitem.title: UK: Stg yet to hurt UK air exports but some yields hit.
newsitem.headline: Stg yet to hurt UK air exports but some yields hit.

text.p: The strength of stg does not yet appear to be affecting UK air cargo exports but the next two months could be critical, said Air Canada cargo general manager for Europe, the Middle East and Africa, Des Vertannes.
"There has been surprising resilience in the export market" and Air Canada has enjoyed relatively good demand, he added.
But the summer months, when several European countries have extended holidays with factory closures, could leave the way open for a drop in UK air cargo exports, he said in an interview.
Air Canada's European statistics show tonnage so far this year running up on last year. Helped by strong stg, Canadian dollar yields from the UK in June were running 16 percent up on last year.
But Ventannes said from European countries whose countries had weakened, the dollar yields were lower.
In some cases -- such as from Frankfurt and Paris -- declines in yields of five and six percent respectively were in fact the result of currency declines of over 10 and eight percent.

Air Canada's Zurich station competes for business to the U.S. where yields are lower than to Canada and this further hit yields, which were 12 percent lower in June than a year ago. -Douglas Learmond, Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
